How to connect AI agents to your tools with MCP, by use case

MCP servers, clients and registries that give agents safe access to your apps and data. We list 3,550 tools for connecting tools with MCP below, each with a link-checked page, pricing as the maker states it and alternatives.

Updated November 25, 2026

3,550 tools: 1,040 open source, 13 source-available, 195 free or freemium, 108 paid, usage-based or enterprise, 2,194 pricing on the maker's site.

Looking for the full list of MCP servers? See the MCP servers category.

On 24 Nov 2026 the pricing page listed a free plan with 60 voice minutes a month and no card. Paid yearly totals were Starter $590 (120 voice minutes), Growth $1,990 (450 voice minutes) and Business $3,750 (950 voice minutes), with the monthly toggle showing $59, $199 and $375. The endpoint is https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp.

The tools are text_to_morse, morse_to_text, morse_audio and morse_alphabet.

Repomix is an MIT-licensed CLI and web tool (repomix.com) that packs a whole repository, local or remote, into one AI-friendly file in XML, Markdown or plain text, so you can hand a codebase to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or a coding agent in one go. It respects .gitignore, shows token counts per file, can compress code to signatures, and scans the output with Secretlint so secrets are not shared. It also runs as an MCP server; v1.19.0 shipped in November 2026.

Fileaify

agent infraFreemium

Fileaify is a project workspace that plugs into the coding agent you already use, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf. You give the agent one URL (fileaify.com/agent) or the hosted MCP connector, approve its access, and it finds the project's documentation, architecture decisions, roadmap and known issues in each new conversation, so you don't have to explain the project again, even when you switch agents. Credentials stay in a vault: the agent can run approved actions with them without ever seeing the keys, sensitive actions need a human's approval, and paid tiers add a sandboxed executor where the agent can actually run work. The agent also writes its contributions back into the project docs, following your review rules. A live demo project lets you try it without installing anything.
